question: Which property makes the Venturi mask a fixed-performance oxygen delivery device?

answers.text: It delivers oxygen at a fixed flow rate set by the flowmeter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Flow rate is set by the clinician, but this alone does not make FiO2 fixed — variable-performance devices also use set flow rates.

answers.text: It entrains a fixed ratio of room air relative to oxygen flow, maintaining a constant FiO2 regardless of the patient's inspiratory flow

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Venturi jet creates a fixed air-entrainment ratio via the Bernoulli/Venturi principle, so the delivered FiO2 is predictable and constant.

answers.text: It has a reservoir bag that stores pre-mixed gas before each inspiration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A reservoir bag is a feature of the non-rebreather mask, not the Venturi mask.

answers.text: It seals tightly against the face, preventing any room-air entrainment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Venturi mask does NOT form an airtight seal — it deliberately allows controlled air entrainment through the jet ports.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Venturi mask section. The key principle is controlled air-entrainment through the jet, yielding a fixed FiO2 independent of patient effort.
Well done. The fixed air-entrainment ratio is the defining feature of Venturi (fixed-performance) devices — this is why they are preferred in COPD where a precise FiO2 is required.
